verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents a self-hosted Edge Proxy that runs the Flagsmith Engine inside your own infrastructure and acts as a local cache, so server-side SDKs evaluate flags against it rather than the Core API. That satisfies the edge/relay-layer form of the story. Missing for 10: any documented CDN-worker or edge-runtime evaluation, evidence of client-side or browser SDKs connecting to the proxy close to end users (the docs frame it as close to your servers), and independent or hands-on corroboration of Edge Proxy deployments.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can evaluate flags at the edge (CDN workers or an edge/relay layer) close to users

citations.quote: The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
Run the Edge Proxy within in your own infrastructure and connect to it from your server-side SDKs
The proxy also acts as a local cache, allowing you to make requests to the proxy without hitting the Core API.
